question.text: Sahyadri Stat-Arb Fund (open-ended Cat III AIF) is declaring First Close. It has received capital commitments of INR 18 crore from anchor investors plus INR 2 crore sponsor contribution. Can it validly declare First Close?

answer.text: Yes; the INR 20 crore total (commitments + sponsor) meets SEBI's minimum corpus requirement at First Close
Yes; any corpus amount is permitted at First Close for open-ended Cat III AIFs
No; the minimum corpus requirement at First Close is INR 50 crore
No; sponsor contribution cannot be counted toward First Close corpus

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI requires that at First Close, corpus of any AIF shall NOT be less than INR 20 crore. The corpus includes committed capital from investors AND sponsor commitment (which is itself a scheme investment). INR 18 cr + INR 2 cr = INR 20 cr meets the threshold. The Trap: Option A ignores the floor. Option C inflates it to INR 50 cr (SIF minimum for Social Impact Funds is INR 5 cr). Option D is wrong — sponsor contribution must be via scheme investment and does count. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D tests the same INR 20 cr for Cat I/II. XIX-E frames it in open-ended Cat III context (First Close = end of Initial Offer Period for open-ended). Manager's Pro-Tip: Once First Close is declared, sponsor commitment cannot be reduced, withdrawn or transferred. Lock the sponsor subscription into the NAV ledger before publicising First Close date.
